objective: Admit auditable route receipts only when requested and effective route facts, approved model/version/provider constraints, fallback depth, trajectory confidence/stability, tool-use state, freshness, generation, and route budget remain within policy.

research_inputs.finding: Agentic confidence is a trajectory-level reliability property affected by compounding step uncertainty, tool/environment uncertainty, and masked intermediate failures; process-level confidence and stability signals are needed for interpretable calibration.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL admits trajectory summaries with confidence, stability, tool uncertainty, step count, and fallback depth thresholds, while treating confidence as evidence rather than truth.

research_inputs.finding: Adaptive routing should produce route receipts that record material requested versus effective route facts, version/alias resolution, service tier, fallback behavior, tool use, and redaction-safe runtime conditions without exposing hidden reasoning or proprietary routing logic.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a portable route-receipt admission contract that verifies approved effective route facts and emits an auditable receipt without selecting models or invoking inference.

features: trajectory step, confidence, stability, tool-uncertainty, and fallback-depth checks
route cost budget, freshness, generation, replay, and intent/session fences
receipt-only output with inference_executed=false and model_selected=false

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane admission overhead; excludes model selection, inference, provider calls, tool execution, network, storage, and production approval latency

limitations: The contract verifies caller-supplied route facts and trajectory summaries; it does not independently observe the serving provider or model runtime.
Confidence and stability values are evidence inputs, not calibrated truth; a trained calibrator and held-out production trajectory labels are not supplied by this contract.
The benchmark does not establish calibration error, routing quality, cost savings, latency improvement, tool success, AGI capability, production efficacy, or Linux superiority.
No physical hardware, external reviewer, independent builder, live multihost environment, or production approval was exercised.

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the route-receipt module, tests, benchmark, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain the memory-intervention release tag
